title: Can a Husband's Loan EMIs Lower His Maintenance?
desc: The Supreme Court held on 16 April 2026, in a case from an Uttarakhand Family Court, that loan EMIs cannot cut a husband's maintenance liability.
why: A Supreme Court ruling this year, arising from a maintenance dispute that began in an Uttarakhand Family Court, now shapes how courts across the state work out how much a husband must pay.
keyPoints: A husband cannot lower his maintenance by pointing to loan EMIs he pays to buy or build assets for himself.
The Supreme Court raised maintenance from Rs 15,000 to Rs 25,000 a month on 16 April 2026 in a case that started in an Uttarakhand Family Court.
The Court called the duty to maintain a spouse a 'primary obligation' that cannot be pushed below voluntary financial commitments.
Courts look at a person's real earning capacity, not merely the income left after such commitments, under section 144 of the BNSS.

sections.h: Does paying loan EMIs reduce how much maintenance you owe?
p: No. A husband cannot reduce the maintenance he pays his wife merely by showing loan EMIs for buying property or other assets. In a case that began in an Uttarakhand Family Court, the Supreme Court raised maintenance from Rs 15,000 to Rs 25,000 a month on 16 April 2026, holding that repayments which create assets are capital in nature, not necessary expenditure, under section 144 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023.

The bench said the duty to maintain a spouse is a 'primary obligation' that cannot be subordinated to a person's own voluntary financial arrangements, however reasonable those arrangements may otherwise seem.

sections.h: How did the maintenance amount rise through the courts?
p: The wife had asked for Rs 50,000 a month. The Family Court awarded Rs 8,000. On appeal, the Uttarakhand High Court raised this to Rs 15,000. The Supreme Court raised it further to Rs 25,000, finding that the lower courts had given too much weight to the husband's loan deductions while working out his real income.
The Court also directed that arrears be cleared within three months, with monthly payments due by the 7th of each month going forward.

sections.h: What counts as income when a court sets maintenance?
p: Courts are expected to look at a person's actual earning capacity, not just the salary left after loan instalments, savings or other voluntary outgoings. Expenses that are truly unavoidable, such as supporting dependants, can be considered, but building personal assets through loans is not treated the same way.

This reasoning applies alongside the interim maintenance process under section 144 BNSS: the stage at which maintenance is fixed, and the way income is assessed, are two separate questions a court must get right.

whatToDo: Keep salary slips, bank statements and loan statements ready, since both sides' real income is central to any maintenance hearing.
If your maintenance was reduced because of loan EMIs you pay, check whether those loans were for buying or building an asset in your own name.
If a Family Court or High Court order feels low or high on this ground, an appeal is possible; take legal advice on your own facts.
Track payment dates and arrears carefully, since recovery applications under section 144 BNSS have their own time limit.

hi.title: क्या लोन की ईएमआई से भरण-पोषण की राशि कम हो सकती है?
keyPoints: पति अपनी संपत्ति बनाने के लिए चुकाई जा रही लोन ईएमआई का हवाला देकर भरण-पोषण की राशि कम नहीं करवा सकता।
उत्तराखंड के एक फैमिली कोर्ट से शुरू हुए मामले में सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने 16 अप्रैल 2026 को भरण-पोषण 15,000 रुपये से बढ़ाकर 25,000 रुपये प्रति माह कर दिया।
अदालत ने कहा कि पति-पत्नी का भरण-पोषण करना एक 'प्राथमिक दायित्व' है, जिसे स्वैच्छिक वित्तीय प्रतिबद्धताओं से कम नहीं आंका जा सकता।
धारा 144 बीएनएसएस के तहत अदालतें व्यक्ति की वास्तविक आय क्षमता देखती हैं, न कि ऐसी प्रतिबद्धताओं के बाद बची राशि।
